system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Subjective-logic fusion of MVFA branches with an explicit uncertainty mass from support size
SUMMARY: Express each branch's per-image evidence as a subjective-logic opinion (belief in abnormal, belief in normal, uncertainty) whose uncertainty mass shrinks as K grows, fuse the two opinions with the cumulative fusion operator, and score images by projected probability while reporting uncertainty.
HYPOTHESIS: Subjective-logic fusion keeps image AUROC within 1 point of log-odds fusion at K >= 4, and its uncertainty mass identifies unreliable decisions: among the 20% of images with the highest uncertainty, the error rate at the support threshold is at least twice that of the remaining images, at every K.
RATIONALE: The log-odds parent produces a single probability per image, which hides how much evidence it rests on; with K = 2 supports the same probability is far less trustworthy than with K = 16. By analogy with evidential reasoning in sensor fusion (Dempster-Shafer, subjective logic), each branch can contribute belief, disbelief and an explicit uncertainty mass determined by its amount of evidence, here the support size and the branch's agreement with its own leave-one-out statistics. Cumulative fusion combines independent opinions, and the resulting uncertainty is a per-image reliability signal that a clinical user can act on.
METHOD: 1) For branch b: evidence counts from the calibrated probability p_b (as in the parent) and support size: r_b = W p_b n_b, s_b = W (1 - p_b) n_b with n_b = K for the few-shot branch and n_0 = 16 (source-calibrated) for the zero-shot branch, W = 2; opinion (b, d, u) = (r, s, W)/(r + s + W). 2) Cumulative fusion of the two opinions (Josang's operator). 3) Score = projected probability b + a u (a = 0.5); report u. 4) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Conditions: log-odds fusion; subjective-logic fusion. Metrics: image AUROC, error rate in the top-20% uncertainty group vs the rest, risk-coverage curve when abstaining on high-uncertainty images, score shift under resampling. Falsified if the high-uncertainty group's error rate is not at least twice the rest's.

Idea B:
TITLE: Conformal few-shot p-values and temperature-calibrated zero-shot probabilities fused in log-odds
SUMMARY: Turn the few-shot branch into a conformal p-value from the leave-one-out support distribution, keep the zero-shot branch as a temperature-calibrated probability, and combine both in log-odds with weights fitted on source episodes.
HYPOTHESIS: Fusing a conformal few-shot p-value with a temperature-calibrated zero-shot probability in log-odds keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4, makes each image's score exactly invariant to the test set, and controls the false-positive rate on normal images at the nominal 5% within 2 points when the few-shot branch alone is thresholded.
RATIONALE: The empirical-CDF parent makes scores test-set-invariant but treats both branches as uncalibrated ranks; the log-odds parent shows that the zero-shot branch is already a probability once a temperature is fitted. The two branches differ in nature: the few-shot score is a distance to supports, for which a rank against leave-one-out support scores is a valid conformal p-value with a finite-sample false-positive guarantee, while the zero-shot score is a classifier output. Treating each by its nature, a p-value for the few-shot branch and a probability for the zero-shot branch, and combining them in log-odds with source-fitted weights preserves the guarantee of the first and the calibration of the second.
METHOD: 1) Few-shot: for each support i, LOO image score r_i (top-1% mean of 1 - max cosine to the bank without i, averaged over levels); test image score s; conformal p = (1 + #{r_i >= s})/(K + 1). 2) Zero-shot: p0 = softmax(T^-1 logits) with T fitted on source validation. 3) Fused logit z = w0 logit(p0) + w1 logit(1 - p) + c, with w0, w1, c fitted by logistic regression on source episodes (50 per source modality, K matched). 4) test_few.py: remove min-max; report thresholded results at p <= 0.05 (few-shot alone) and at z = 0. 5) Pixel maps: the same transform per pixel using LOO pixel reference sets subsampled to 10^5 values. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) conformal few-shot alone, (ii) + calibrated zero-shot with average fusion, (iii) log-odds fusion with source weights. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, realised FPR at p <= 0.05, ECE, score shift under resampling. Falsified if AUROC drops more than 1 point or realised FPR at nominal 5% exceeds 7%.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
